findings.claim: The recorded G-STEM major flag states a blind-leak mechanism that is demonstrably false — C is NOT the only hedged option — and no review record shows any stage adjudicated the flag, even though GENERATION.md law 10 assigns exactly this judgment to pedagogy-review.
findings.evidence: verdicts.jsonl / report.json, G-STEM q:1, severity major: "The stem's framing ('implied', 'that ball makers advertise') primes a debunking key, which C supplies as the only hedged option ('can be smaller than')." Option A reads "That deeper dimples tend to give a longer flight than shallow ones at the same speed." — 'tend to' is a hedge, so C is one of two hedged options, not the only one. The unit's own hedge_balance_note says so: "Two options carry hedges ('tend to' in A, 'can be' in C) ... so neither 'strip the absolutes' nor 'pick the qualified answer' isolates the key". GENERATION.md law 10 on the sole-hedged-key correlation says "(This is judgment `pedagogy-review` audits; it is not mechanically gated.)" — and reviews/pedagogy.jsonl carries only {"verdict":"MINOR_FIXES"} with no findings field.
findings.why: Not verdict-changing, and the error runs in the conservative direction: the flag survives on its other two legs (D is an eliminable absolute — "has no bearing" — and the golf-aerodynamics world knowledge that makes A false), and BATCH-RUNBOOK.md line 162 records the contract as "structural-leak/recall = kill, world-knowledge = flag", so SURVIVED_FLAGGED is the right disposition. My own blind pass on the options alone still leans C, but via a different path than the gate names — eliminate D as an absolute and A as off-stem (it speaks to depth, which the passage explicitly separates from pattern), leaving C vs a substantive B. Recorded because a major flag's stated mechanism is partly false and nothing downstream corrects it.

findings.claim: The rationale's derivation story overclaims: it presents C as a three-part synthesis anchored on the twelve-micron tolerance figure, but C follows from the same-box sentence alone — the twelve-micron figure is not load-bearing for the key.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "it reports that depth is what the tunnel notices, that twelve microns of depth is inside the drift of a mould across one production run, and that 'two balls lifted from the same box can differ more, in the tunnel, than two rival designs differ on paper'. Putting those together gives C". generator_meta.key_derivation repeats it: "one_inch_inference — the twelve-micron tolerance figure read together with the same-box comparison". Key C is "That the gap between rival patterns can be smaller than the variation inside one box." — a direct transposition of the quoted same-box sentence (same-box difference > rival-design difference => rival-design gap < same-box variation). Delete the twelve-micron sentence from the passage and C is unchanged in support. The header phrase "one logical inch beyond the tunnel's two findings" is loose in the same way: the tunnel yields three reported findings (depth sensitivity, mould drift, same-box comparison), only one of which the key uses.
findings.why: Not a key defect and not double-keying — the real inference step C does require is small but genuine (the passage compares tunnel-measured variation against an on-paper design difference; C drops 'on paper' and generalises to the actual gap, which the text licenses via "the patterns matter less than the catalogues suggest" and the hedge "can be"). Law 3 is also satisfied: C recasts the sentence in wholly different words (gap / rival patterns / variation / one box), so the family calibration rule "om alternativet förekommer ordagrant i passagen är det INTE implikations-svaret" is not tripped. Recorded because the rationale is the student-facing teaching payload and it credits a figure that does no work, which is exactly the pedagogy stage's remit.

findings.claim: The trap label on distractor B does not name the trap its own justification describes: the label says "reversed relationship" while the justification's decisive clause describes an unsupported claim.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "B = reversed relationship; the mould appears in the passage as the source of the drift that swamps the design, never as a criterion the makers design around, and nothing is said about how patterns are chosen." B reads "That makers pick their patterns to survive the wear of the moulds they are pressed in." The passage's only mould content is "twelve microns is inside the drift of a mould across a single production run" — it never says makers choose patterns for any reason, and never uses 'wear'. "nothing is said about how patterns are chosen" is the signature of the family's "Två-stegs-hopp (rimligt men ostött)" pattern in elf/families.json, not of "Inferens i omvänd riktning". The same soft mismatch appears on A, whose "too_far" label is followed by a second, different refutation: "the stem asks what is implied about the advertised patterns, which A never speaks to" (off-stem, not over-extrapolation).
findings.why: Both labels are defensible on their first clause — B does invert the mould/design direction of influence (noise that swamps design vs constraint the design answers to), and A does extend a one-directional depth finding into a monotonic law — so no distractor is mislabelled outright and neither becomes defensible. Recorded because 'trap labels name the actual trap' is the integrated stage's own check and both labels are less precise than their accompanying prose.

findings.claim: The three review records are verdict-only, so no recorded verdict can be falsified from the records themselves; I audited the artifacts instead, and the artifacts substantiate all three verdicts.
findings.evidence: reviews/{language,pedagogy,integrated}.jsonl lines for elf-b12-004 carry only candidate_id, stage, verdict, reviewed_by, date. Artifact trail: candidates/elf-b12-004.json and candidates-corrected/elf-b12-004.json are byte-identical (diff empty), consistent with language CLEAR making no edits; candidates-corrected/ -> candidates-final/ is a rationale-only rewrite of the A-refutation, from "the passage says a dimple shallower by twelve microns behaves almost like no dimple, which establishes that depth matters near a threshold" to "the passage's depth finding runs in one direction only ... which establishes that small losses of depth have outsized effects, not that flight keeps lengthening as dimples get deeper; and the stem asks what is implied about the advertised patterns, which A never speaks to" — consistent with pedagogy MINOR_FIXES / integrated MINOR_NOTES, and student-facing text was untouched so no re-gate was owed under the runbook. Independent checks all pass: every quoted span in the rationale is verbatim in the shipped passage ('two balls lifted from the same box can differ more, in the tunnel, than two rival designs differ on paper', 'hexagonal packing does buy a little' + 'at the margins' across the ellipsis, 'no bearing', 'tend to', 'can be'); BrE is held throughout student-facing text ('metres', 'mould'/'moulds', 'catalogues') with no AmE forms in passage or options, and 'moulds' in option B carries the variety into the options; anti-tell holds by word count (A=16, B=16, C=15, D=15, key joint-shortest, matching the rationale's "15 words against 16/16/15"); the byline form "— Halvard Ekstrand, science pages" matches the sibling convention in this batch ("— Petra Vanterpool, consumer affairs", "— Odile Brennan, design notebook") and is publication-neutral per elf/anti-plagiarism.md; single question, so no cross-question leak is possible; and the key is uniquely defensible — D is contradicted by "hexagonal packing does buy a little, she thinks, at the margins", B invents a selection criterion the text never states, and A is both off-stem and unsupported since the passage never compares deeper against shallower balls in flight.
findings.why: Record-format observation only, matching the same gap noted in batches 11 and earlier. One further non-defect worth logging rather than raising: the passage's central figure is hyperbolic against the real world — real dimple depth is on the order of 150 microns, so a 12-micron shortfall behaving "almost like no dimple at all" is a large exaggeration — but it is an invented facility's finding about a single dimple (the noun is singular), G-ENG passed 3-0 and G-REGISTER passed, no law forbids implausible fictional measurements, and the exaggeration cannot move a solver off C.
